subject: Non-disruptive switchover metrics and validation guidance
messages:

Cc: Mark Benson <mark.benson@trufin.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Non-disruptive switchover metrics — additional details requested

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the overview in the RFP response. A couple of follow-ups from our DR/compliance team so we can finalize acceptance criteria for the procurement:

- We need a concise statement of expected RTO and RPO for the inference endpoints and for dependent state (KV cache, audit logs). Please call out what you commit to for production cutovers vs. best-effort.
- For multi-region failover, what traffic steering approach do you recommend (DNS TTL, Anycast, load balancer east-west)? What TTLs or propagation windows should we plan for?
- We expect the failover to be non-disruptive for 95% of requests. How do you measure and validate that during a rehearsal (example metrics, thresholds, and tooling)?
- Can you provide a sample replication-lag export and a copy/section of the switchover runbook you follow during rehearsals?

We have a target dry-run window the week of Oct 4th; please confirm availability and any blackout windows required on your side.

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Park
Director, Resilience & Compliance
TruFin Capital

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Non-disruptive switchover metrics — additional details requested

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Marcus will follow up with concrete metrics and a sample CSV. I'm attaching the current switchover-playbook-v2.pdf (redacted for customer distribution) to give you the rehearsal sequence.

High-level:
- RTO / RPO: we design for rapid control-plane failover and graceful data-plane migration. Typical operational targets we validate in rehearsals are RTO <= 5 minutes and RPO <= 30 seconds for request-serving continuity; persistent telemetry/log buckets may have RPO up to 5 minutes depending on region. Marcus will provide measured examples.
- Traffic steering: preferred approach is weighted DNS with short TTLs (30–60s) combined with a brief canary shift and health-probe checks to avoid bulk flapping. We can support Anycast or cloud LB-based active-active if you require it.
- Validation methodology: rehearsals follow a staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated SLO checks for error rate, p95 latency, and successful model load. We log a replication-lag metric during the run and stop progression on breach.

See attached playbook excerpt for roles and approval gates. Marcus — can you add the CSV sample and replication-lag extraction steps?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: switchover-playbook-v2.pdf (excerpt)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Non-disruptive switchover metrics — technical details and sample

Hi Alyssa,

Per Neha, attaching a short sample export (cross-region-replication-lag-sample.csv) and documenting the measured behavior we run in dry-runs. Notes below are operational best-practices we follow in production and in customer rehearsals.

Measured targets we validate during rehearsals (example values we have achieved in prior customer dry-runs):
- Control-plane cutover (orchestration + routing policy change): median 20–40s, 95th percentile 90s. We treat <2 minutes as our operational SLO for control-plane RTO in planned failovers.
- Data-plane continuity (in-flight requests and model availability): typical session continuity >95% for endpoints when using staged canary; p95 latency increase <= 15%.
- RPO (request-serving critical data): near-zero for read-only model artifacts; for ephemeral KV caches we target RPO <= 30s with asynchronous cross-region replication and prefix/KV cache warming during canary.
- Persistent logs/metrics: best-effort replication with RPO <= 5 minutes; we surface any delayed batches in the runbook.

Traffic steering and DNS strategy:
- Primary recommendation: weighted DNS with TTL 30s. Canary schedule: 0% -> 5% (10 minutes) -> 25% (15 minutes) -> 100% (monitor for 30 minutes).
- If you control global BGP/Anycast, we can integrate route withdrawals for faster convergence, but that requires network ops coordination.
- Circuit breakers: auto-fallback after threshold breach (error rate > 2% or p95 latency > 2x baseline) to previous stable region; this prevents noisy cutovers.

Replication-lag instrumentation and sample CSV content (attached):
- We sample the last 30 minutes of replication offset for each shard and include wall-clock vs. commit-timestamp, average lag, and 99th percentile lag.
- During rehearsals we push synthetic writes and validate that lag converges to expected values before moving from 5% -> 25%.

Test run steps (abbreviated):
1) Pre-run: warm caches, validate model weights checksum, snapshot offset markers.
2) Start canary: shift 5% traffic; run synthetic test suite for 10 minutes.
3) Observe metrics: error rate, p95 latency, replication lag.
4) Advance or rollback based on gate thresholds.
5) Post-run: collect artifacts (metrics, logs, replication offsets) into an evidence package.

Attachments: cross-region-replication-lag-sample.csv (sample), excerpted metric queries.

If you want, we can prepare a runbook slice that maps directly to your audit checklist and include pre-signed attestations for the rehearsal.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — that helps. A few follow-ups before we schedule:

- Can you provide the acceptance thresholds in a simple table we can insert into our audit (error rate, p95 latency delta, replication-lag 99th pct)?
- For the Oct 4th window we requested a 2-week change-freeze on our side; will Redwood require any internal blackout or capacity reservations?
- Please include the canary-checklist.xlsx (we need the exact gating time windows so our SREs can coordinate).

Also, for compliance we need a short paragraph describing how you capture and retain evidence (metrics + logs + timestamps) after a rehearsal and how long artifacts are stored for audit.

If you can confirm the Oct 5th dry-run (Oct 4th reserve day for prep) and send the checklist we can lock in resources.

Regards,
Alyssa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Non-disruptive switchover metrics — technical details and sample

Alyssa — confirmed. We can reserve Oct 4 for prep and run the dry-run on Oct 5 (US primetime). Action items we completed/attached:

- Attached: canary-checklist.xlsx (gating windows and exact thresholds), switchover-playbook-v2.pdf (annotated), cross-region-replication-lag-sample.csv.
- Acceptance thresholds (quick summary): error rate increase <= 2% vs baseline; p95 latency delta <= +15%; replication-lag 99th percentile <= 60s for KV shards; control-plane RTO target <= 120s. Full table is in the checklist.
- Blackout/ reservations: we recommend a soft reservation on capacity (ability to burst an extra 20% for 30 minutes) to avoid throttles during warm-up; no hard blackout required from Redwood side beyond our engineering on-call for the rehearsal.
- Evidence retention: rehearsal artifacts (metrics snapshots, offsets, logs, and a signed runbook excerpt) are collected automatically and stored in a customer evidence bundle. We retain that bundle for 90 days by default; longer retention can be arranged via an add-on. Each artifact includes UTC timestamps and checksums; we can provide a signed manifest for audits.

Next steps: I'll upload the annotated playbook and checklist to the HubSpot engagement and share links. If Oct 5 works for you, I'll schedule a 60-minute runbook walk-through with our SREs on Oct 1.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
